nodes.title: Localised Hasse injection
nodes.statement: Let a weight-one modular ρ at tame N have distinct nonzero p-Frobenius roots α,β. Localise the coherent weight-one space M at its away-p ideal, with T_p−(α+β) and 〈p〉−αβ nilpotent on the whole localised module. For a suitable positive power A of the Hasse invariant, of weight h divisible by p−1 and h+1≥2, with the torsion-coefficient sufficient-power conditions below, the composite M→H⁰(ω^{h+1})_m→H⁰(ω^{h+1})_{β,m} is injective. The second map is projection to the generalized U_p=β summand. The assertion holds with torsion O/π^a coefficients and for either root; away-p Hecke actions commute with it.
hypotheses: p∤N; actual tame coherent coefficient modules and q-expansion principle, with fine level or the supplier’s stack descent.
α≠β and αβ≠0; the source operators T_p−(α+β) and 〈p〉−αβ are nilpotent on the entire localized module.

Over O/π^a choose a lift A of a Hasse power, weight h divisible by p−1, q-expansion 1 modulo π^a, and p^h=0 in O/π^a. Ensure the away-p cyclotomic weight factor is trivial modulo π^a on the relevant Hecke indices. These sufficient-power hypotheses come from R15.3/weight-one-tp-with-torsion-coefficients.
The non-Eisenstein localization makes the source cuspidal; target T_p=U_p follows from p^h=0, rather than from h+1≥2 alone.
proofSteps: Reduce injectivity on torsion coefficients to injectivity on the local socle over k.
Use Hasse’s unchanged q-expansion and split the ordinary target into α and β generalized summands.
A kernel element can be moved down the nilpotent filtration to satisfy UF=αF and VF=βF.
The smallest nonzero exponent of a cuspidal q-expansion contradicts VF=βF.
acceptance: A zero root prevents inversion of U_p.
Equal roots prevent the two-projector argument.
Multiplication by Hasse is not confused with the projection; both arrows appear.
Weight two by itself does not kill p^{weight−1} on O/π^a when a is large; a sufficient Hasse power is required.

nodes.title: Congruent nebentypus at fixed level
nodes.statement: Let ℓ≥5 and f be a normalized cuspidal eigenform of weight k and level Γ1(N), with irreducible residual representation at λ. If ε′ is a characteristic-zero character modulo N congruent to ε modulo λ and with ε′(−1)=(−1)^k, then a weight-k eigenform of the same level and character ε′ gives the same residual representation after coefficient extension. In particular one can replace ℓ-primary character factors by their canonical prime-to-ℓ lift in this range. The fixed-level fixed-character conclusion is not extended to ℓ=2 or 3.
hypotheses: ℓ≥5, irreducible residual representation, compatible parity and congruent characters.
Coefficient fields and λ are retained throughout; characters of ℓ-power order are not themselves trivial in characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Use integral character eigenspaces and the supplied Hecke-localisation comparison.
Compare their residual support using congruence of characters.
Lift a common residual eigencharacter in the required characteristic-zero character component.
acceptance: A character of order ℓ reduces to one but can be nontrivial before reduction.
At ℓ=3 the level-13 weight-two character obstruction is retained.
Parity is a hypothesis rather than a consequence of arbitrary residual congruence.

nodes.title: Stripping coefficient-prime powers from level

The conclusion preserves the residual representation and the prime-to-ℓ level, while allowing weight, characteristic-zero nebentypus, coefficient field and coefficient prime to change. Dyadic stripping is supplied by the separate Buzzard weight/level bridge, not by this theorem.

nodes.title: First character normalization
nodes.statement: For odd ℓ write the coefficient-prime nebentypus as ηω^i with η of ℓ-power order. Choose ξ of ℓ-power order with ξ²=η^{-1}. The twist f⊗ξ gives the same residual representation and character εω^i. Choose r′≥r so that cond(ξ)² divides ℓ^{r′}; the twisted witness is on Γ0(ℓ^{r′})∩Γ1(ℓN). The twist can increase the initial ℓ-depth, which subsequent steps then remove.

The global Dirichlet twist has only ℓ-power conductor; its level bound includes the square of that conductor.

nodes.title: Teichmüller character removal
nodes.statement: Choose a positive exponent i representing the Teichmüller character. The Eisenstein form G of type (i,ω^{-i}) at Γ0(ℓ) has constant term c=L(1−i,ω^{-i})/2 with negative λ-valuation. Kummer congruences and the von Staudt calculation give this valuation, while the positive coefficients are integral. Thus E=c^{-1}G is integral and E≡1 modulo λ. Multiplication by E removes ω^i and preserves the residual q-expansion at Γ0(ℓ^{r′})∩Γ1(N), in increased weight. Lift the resulting good-prime residual eigencharacter; the product need not be a characteristic-zero eigenform.
hypotheses: Compatible parity and the Eisenstein congruence of Ribet’s proof.
proofSteps: Use the supplied primitive Eisenstein-series normalization and the special L-value valuation congruence to construct E≡1.
Use the q-expansion principle to identify the product’s residual good-prime Hecke support.
Apply the finite-free eigenvalue-lifting contract, allowing coefficients and weight to change.
acceptance: Multiplication changes the weight.
Congruence of q-expansions is not an automatic assertion about all bad-prime Hecke operators.

nodes.title: Reducing coefficient-prime depth
nodes.statement: For r′>1, take a finite Galois coefficient field K and σ in its λ-decomposition group inducing residue Frobenius a↦a^ℓ. The characteristic-zero form σ^{-1}f is of the same weight and level, with its character conjugated. Then g=(σ^{-1}f)^ℓ|U_ℓ is a cusp form on Γ0(ℓ^{r′−1})∩Γ1(N); modulo λ its q-expansion equals that of f. Iterate to depth one, retaining the original residue embedding and good-prime eigencharacter.

Characteristic-zero coefficient Galois stability from current ModularForms layer 8G.
The source’s level-depth U_ℓ property at r′>1; a characteristic-p V operator alone does not supply it.

nodes.title: The trace step at coefficient-prime level
nodes.statement: At depth one and tame character ε, use the partial Atkin–Lehner operator W with W²=ε(ℓ). On weight-w forms the trace is Tr(F)=F+ε(ℓ)^{-1}ℓ^{1−w/2}F|W|U_ℓ. Let E≡1 be the level-one Eisenstein form of weight a=ℓ−1 for ℓ>3, or a=4 for ℓ=3. Put g=E−ℓ^{a/2}E|W=E−ℓ^aE|V_ℓ. Then g≡1 and v_ℓ(g|W)≥1+a/2. For sufficiently large i the nonidentity trace term of f g^i has positive λ-valuation, so Tr(f g^i) is a level-N cusp form congruent to f. Lift its residual good-prime eigencharacter.
hypotheses: The source’s partial W at Γ1(N)∩Γ0(ℓ), with tame character ε, W²=ε(ℓ), and the normalized V/U operators.
Integral q-expansions and bounded denominators of f|W; choose i so 1−(k+ia)/2+v_ℓ(f|W)+i(1+a/2)>0.
proofSteps: Import the normalized partial Atkin–Lehner and trace formulas from current ModularForms layers 3 and 6.
Construct g using layer 0 Eisenstein forms and compute its positive W-valuation.
The displayed exponent tends to infinity with i, so the nonidentity trace term vanishes modulo λ.
Use the q-expansion principle and eigenvalue lifting on the level-N cusp lattice.
acceptance: Choosing i too small can leave a nonzero Fricke contribution.
The target weight and character may change.

nodes.title: Weight two at level Nℓ
nodes.statement: Let ℓ≥3, ℓ∤N, 2≤k≤ℓ+1 and ρ an irreducible eigensystem at tame level N. If ℓ>3 or N>3, it occurs in weight two at level Nℓ. The geometric bridge uses coefficient-prime character ω^{k−2} and a tame characteristic-zero character reducing to the original ε; at ℓ≥5 the canonical prime-to-ℓ lift of ε can be prescribed using Carayol. At ℓ=3 no unconditional fixed characteristic-zero tame character is asserted. At k=ℓ+1 distinguish genuine filtration ℓ+1, realized by the special-fibre differential bridge with trivial ℓ-character, from a Hasse multiple of weight two, lifted first at N and included as an oldform at Nℓ. Occurrence is the conclusion, not universal exact newness at ℓ.
hypotheses: 2≤k≤ℓ+1, irreducible ρ, ℓ∤N.
ℓ>3 or N>3; coefficient field enlarged to contain ω.
proofSteps: For 3≤k≤ℓ apply the small-Katz-weight/weight-two geometric bridge with its Teichmüller and residue character.
For genuine filtration ℓ+1 use Gross Proposition 8.18’s special-fibre differential realization and Proposition 9.3(2); do not deduce a tame-level weight-two witness in this nonfinite branch.
For weight two or a weight-ℓ+1 Hasse multiple of it, lift at tame level and include it at Nℓ.
Lift eigenvalues without fixing a characteristic-zero tame character at ℓ=3; at ℓ≥5 use the separate character-replacement theorem.
acceptance: For k=2 the coefficient-prime character is trivial.
For k=ℓ+1 the exponent ℓ−1 is trivial, but the Hasse boundary is still checked.
Do not assert exact new level Nℓ.
At ℓ=3 only reduction of the tame character is prescribed; Gross’s level-13 obstruction prevents an arbitrary fixed characteristic-zero lift.

nodes.statement: Let ℓ≥5 and ρ be continuous odd irreducible and already modular, finite flat over Z_ℓ at ℓ, with det ρ on inertia equal to χ_ℓ. The recipe implication from finite-flatness and determinant is supplied by R15.4/R07.5; the application here combines it with level and character optimisation.

Use the supplier’s recipe comparison; no arbitrary finite-image implication.

nodes.title: Buzzard’s global multiplicity-one condition
nodes.statement: For a dyadic irreducible modular ρ, Buzzard multiplicity one means the following universal condition. For every Γ with Γ1(M)⊆Γ⊆Γ0(M) and every full weight-two Picard Hecke ideal m giving ρ, dim_{T/m}J(Γ)[m]=2, where M is odd if ρ is finite flat at 2 and v_2(M)=1 otherwise. The universal quantification is over all these levels and groups, not one optimal level. The Hecke algebra includes all T_n and diamonds, and the residual Picard representation is identified with ρ using its actual dual/twist normalization.
hypotheses: Irreducible modular ρ in characteristic two; finite-flat branch fixed.
Jacobian torsion, full integral Hecke algebra and residue embedding are supplied by R14.3.
J[m] is actual residue torsion of the Jacobian, unlike an O-free cohomology lattice.
proofSteps: Use the supplied full Hecke action and Picard residual normalization.
Define the all-level condition with the correct parity of M.
Prove Γ1(M) suffices because the intermediate-Jacobian map has only abelian kernel action, hence no irreducible ρ contribution.
acceptance: A single m with dimension two does not establish the global condition.
Omitting T_2 can increase the isotypic multiplicity.
Scalar local Frobenius may violate this condition.

nodes.title: Nonscalar dyadic multiplicity one
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an irreducible modular representation in characteristic two. If its restriction to a decomposition group at two is not contained in the scalar matrices, then it satisfies Buzzard’s global multiplicity-one condition at every permitted level and intermediate group. The hypothesis concerns the whole local representation: it includes an unramified nontrivial Jordan block even when the two Frobenius roots coincide. The finite-flat branch uses odd levels; the nonfinite branch uses levels exactly divisible by two.
hypotheses: An actual modularity witness and irreducibility in characteristic two.
The full local restriction at two is nonscalar, without replacing it by its semisimplification.
Full Picard Hecke ideals and the finite-flat/nonfinite level convention of the preceding definition.
proofSteps: Reduce every intermediate group to Γ1(M) by Lemma 2.3; keep the quantification over all permitted M.

For nonfinite ρ and M=2N, adapt Mazur–Ribet’s weight-two argument using the odd-index Hecke ring and w_2; w_2=−U_2 on the two-new part and the Eisenstein component-group input supply its required axioms.

For finite-flat ρ at odd M, use the finite-flat local filtration and the multiplicity argument of Edixhoven Theorem 9.2(2)–(3). Buzzard treats the remaining unramified nondiagonalisable case using the nonsplit sequence (9.2.1); do not discard that extension by semisimplifying.
Transport the resulting two-dimensional full-Hecke Picard torsion to each permitted intermediate group with the imported residual normalization.
acceptance: An unramified Jordan matrix with repeated nonzero root satisfies the nonscalar hypothesis.
A scalar unramified local restriction has no conclusion from this theorem.
A dimension-two factor at one level alone does not establish the universal conclusion.

nodes.title: Buzzard’s auxiliary-prime removal
nodes.statement: If an irreducible mod-two ρ is not induced from Q(i), there are primes r∤2M with r≡3 mod 4 and tr ρ(Frob_r)≠0. For a weight-two witness at level Mr whose r-component character reduces trivially, character normalization and the parity at r make that character odd-order and hence trivial. An unramified-special r-component would have scalar semisimplification and trace zero in characteristic two; therefore the witness is old at r and descends to M while preserving a_2 modulo the coefficient prime.

Weight two and the source’s congruent-character setup; all coefficient primes tracked.

Normalize the character and use r≡3 mod 4 and even weight.
Exclude the special local type by its trace-zero reduction, then remove the old prime.

nodes.title: Carayol’s character lemma mod two
nodes.statement: Let ρ be irreducible mod two and not induced from Q(i), arising from a weight-two characteristic-zero form at level M and character χ. For any character ψ modulo M congruent to χ with ψ(−1)=1, there is a weight-two form of the same level and character ψ giving ρ, and its a_2 is congruent to the original a_2. The parity and non-Q(i)-induced hypotheses are essential parts of this dyadic character-replacement statement.

ρ not Q(i)-induced; ψ(−1)=1.

The new r-character has odd order and trivial reduction.
Remove r by the auxiliary-prime lemma, preserving a_2.

A 2-primary character can reduce to one without being trivial.

nodes.title: Buzzard’s mod-two lowering theorem
nodes.statement: Let q∤2M and f be a normalized weight-two form on Γ1(M)∩Γ0(q), with absolutely irreducible residual ρ. Assume ρ is unramified at q, satisfies Buzzard’s global multiplicity-one condition, and is not induced from Q(i). Require M odd when ρ is finite flat at 2 and v_2(M)=1 otherwise. Then ρ arises from a weight-two form at level M, with a_2 congruent to that of f. The unramifiedness hypothesis is added explicitly: it is used by the published proof but omitted from the printed statement of Theorem 2.8.
hypotheses: q∤2M; ρ unramified at q; absolute irreducibility.
Global multiplicity one; correct dyadic level parity; non-Q(i)-induced representation.
Coefficient DVR extension and residue embedding are allowed.
proofSteps: Normalize characters with the dyadic Carayol lemma, preserving a₂.
If Frobenius at the removed q is nonscalar, use the Γ1(M)∩Γ0(q) bad-fibre torus and Eisenstein component-group comparison; unramifiedness identifies the residual torsion with its reduction.
In the scalar-q case, raise at an auxiliary r with involution Frobenius using the dyadic a₂-preserving milestone. Assuming no descent at q forces qr-new support.
Use the Γ1 false-point discriminant-qr Shimura Jacobian and the requested integral sequence 0→Y_q→L_r→X_r→0. Absence of descent gives (X_r)_m=0.

Global multiplicity one and the involution Frobenius at r bound dim(L_r/mL_r)≤1. Unramifiedness, nonzero quaternionic support and Eisenstein component terms give dim(Y_q/mY_q)≥2. Exact localization identifies these residue spaces, a contradiction.
Lift the lower-level full-Hecke support, retaining a₂; no odd-characteristic splitting inequality is reused.

The ℓ=2 proof does not assume +1 and −1 are distinct.
The output preserves a_2 modulo the coefficient prime.

If the initial witness has odd level, a_2 can be preserved modulo the coefficient prime. nodes.title: Buzzard’s combined weight and level theorem
nodes.statement: For irreducible modular mod-two ρ satisfying Buzzard multiplicity one, there is a characteristic-zero normalized eigenform at its prime-to-two conductor N in weight two if ρ is finite flat at 2 and weight three otherwise. In the Q(i)-induced case lift the inducing odd-order character to a classical weight-one form of level 4N and apply the dyadic bridge directly; this does not invoke Theorem 2.8 on a representation it excludes. In the other case apply conductor lowering and the bridge. Classical even Serre weight four in the nonfinite branch is obtained by a Hasse-weight change, with its character conventions retained.
